chunks: The Sheikh — may God, the Exalted, support him — informed me. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abd Allah (AS):
And he was asked about water in which animals urinate, dogs lap, and a person in a state of janaba bathes. He said: "If the water is the measure of a kurr, nothing can render it impure."

key_terms.الدَّوَابُّ: riding animals and livestock (specifically those that urinate in the water)
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in a state of janaba (major ritual impurity), obligating ghusl before worship
key_terms.كُرٍّ: kurr — the canonical minimum water volume (~384 litres / 36 cubic spans) below which water can become najis
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: to render it najis — to cause ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, at what volume of water does it become impossible for anything — including animal urine, dog saliva, or contact with a person in a state of janaba — to render it ritually impure?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about water in which animals urinate, dogs lap, and a person in a state of janaba (major ritual impurity) bathes. The Imam issues the foundational Shia jurisprudential ruling: if the water reaches the volume of a kurr (a canonical measure of approximately 384 litres), nothing whatsoever can render it ritually impure (najis), regardless of contact with normally impure substances.
